title: Get Paid to Post TikTok Videos: What Actually Pays, What's Clickbait, and How to Start
summary: TikTok's own payout program isn't the same as getting paid to post. Compare flat-fee, per-view, and affiliate deals, vet an offer before you accept, and see what a first paid post really earns.
body_markdown:
## From Zero to First Paid Post: The Step-by-Step Playbook


Your first paid post starts with a focused offer, not a high follower count or a comment that says “Interested.” Decide what you can produce, find opportunities that fit your format, and make your work easy to assess. If your goal is to get paid to post tiktok videos, prioritize clear terms and a manageable first assignment over promises of fast income.


### Winning a Flooded Opportunity Thread Without Spamming 'Interested'


A one-word reply gives a business little reason to choose you. Send a short introduction, a specific content idea, and one relevant example of your work. Without a portfolio, make a sample using a product you already own and label it as a sample, not a paid collaboration. Follow the application instructions and send one thoughtful follow-up through the contact method provided.


Before pitching, review your recent videos for clear audio, readable captions, steady framing, and a strong opening. ### A Short Pitch Template You Can Copy


Personalize each application. Name the deliverable you can provide and ask the business to confirm the scope before you begin. Do not claim results you cannot verify or promise views you cannot control.


> Hi \[Name\], I create \[format or topic\] videos and can produce a \[specific video concept\] for \[product\]. My sample is here: \[link\]. Please share the deliverables, fee, usage rights, revision terms, and payment timeline so I can confirm fit. Thanks, \[Name\]


### Realistic Month-One Earnings and What to Charge Per Video as a Small Creator


Month one is about building proof of skill and securing a first assignment, not relying on a steady income stream. Set a rate by estimating production time, revisions, product costs, and the value of usage rights. If the scope demands more, negotiate or decline.


1. Choose one content format and prepare two or three relevant samples.
2. Apply to opportunities with clear products, deliverables, and business contacts.
3. Confirm the fee, rights, approval process, and payment date in writing.
4. Deliver the agreed work, save the approved version, and request permission to add it to your portfolio.
